meta.origin: LandLord ultracode Opus workflow (per-domain design -> adversarial verify -> synthesis; 22 agents)
meta.kind: general reference PM task-and-process library (a factory asset; a firm's real catalog still loads at the data gate)
meta.note: catalog rows map to CatalogRow (key/title/class/mode/domain/system/completes/params; prevalence is extra, informational). grammars use general ROLE names a setting maps to real seats/holders before loading as FlowTemplates.

grammars.title: Vendor Dispatch (Work Order)
grammars.trigger: A maintenance issue requires a trade vendor to repair it.
grammars.note: The workhorse repair flow. Bound by most maintenance leaves, parameterized by {trade}, {urgency}, and NTE {amount}.

steps.note: Tenant or PM reports the {trade} problem with description and photos.
Diagnose, set {urgency}, and confirm landlord (not tenant-caused) responsibility.
If the estimate exceeds {amount}, route to the owner-approval flow before proceeding.
Select a {trade} vendor and issue the work order with scope and NTE {amount}.
Vendor coordinates access with the tenant within the {urgency} window.
Vendor completes the repair and documents it with photos and notes.
Confirm the work resolved the issue and follow up with the tenant.
Vendor submits the invoice against the work order.
Approve against NTE {amount} and pay the vendor from the property ledger.
Post the cost to the owner ledger and close the work order.

grammars.title: Emergency Response
grammars.trigger: An after-hours or urgent habitability/safety emergency is reported (flood, no heat, gas, security).
grammars.note: Urgent variant of dispatch: mitigate first, approval waived for safety, permanent repair follows.

steps.note: Emergency {trade} issue reported to the after-hours line; capture nature and safety risk.
On-call coordinator assesses life-safety; escalate to 911/utility if warranted.
Dispatch the nearest on-call {trade} vendor with emergency NTE {amount}.
Vendor stabilizes to stop damage and restore safety (may be temporary).
Inform the owner of the emergency and action taken (approval waived for safety).
Schedule any permanent repair as a standard work order.
Process the emergency invoice and post to the owner ledger.
Document the incident and close.

grammars.title: Preventive / Recurring Service
grammars.trigger: A scheduled recurring service is due (HVAC seasonal, filters, gutters, detectors).
grammars.note: Cadence-driven upkeep; parameterized by {trade} and {days} cadence. Spins off work orders for deficiencies found.

steps.note: The recurring schedule generates the {trade} PM task on its {days}-day cadence.
Assign to the PM vendor with the service checklist.
Vendor coordinates tenant access.
Complete the checklist and note any deficiencies found.
Review findings and spin off work orders for any repairs needed.
Pay the flat {amount} and post to the owner ledger.
Close and reset the next cycle.

grammars.title: Service-Request Triage
grammars.trigger: A tenant submits a service/maintenance request.
grammars.note: The intake router that fans requests into emergency-response, vendor-dispatch, or a tenant reply. Reusable as the front door to all maintenance.

steps.note: Tenant submits the request with description, {urgency}, and photos.
Classify as emergency, standard repair, tenant-responsibility, or non-issue.
Determine landlord vs tenant responsibility and check any warranty/home-warranty coverage.
Route to emergency-response, vendor-dispatch, or reply to the tenant.
Acknowledge to the tenant with the expected timeline.

grammars.title: Owner Approval for Spend
grammars.trigger: A repair or expense estimate exceeds the management agreement's approval threshold {amount}.
grammars.note: A reusable approval gate embedded by dispatch, turns, and capital-project flows.

steps.note: Assemble scope, estimate {amount}, photos, and a recommendation.
Send the owner the approval request with the estimate and options.
Owner approves, declines, or requests changes / more bids.
Record the decision; if approved, release the work to proceed.
Hand back to the originating flow, or close if declined.

grammars.title: Capital Project Bidding
grammars.trigger: A larger repair or improvement (roof, unit reno, sewer) warrants competitive bids.
grammars.note: Multi-bid procurement for high-dollar work; owner selects among bids before award.

steps.note: Define the {trade} project scope and requirements.
Request three bids from qualified {trade} vendors.
Vendors submit itemized bids.
Compare bids and prepare a recommendation for the owner.
Owner selects a bid and authorizes the {amount} spend.
Award the job and issue the contract / work order.
Oversee the project through milestones to completion.
Inspect the completed work before final payment.
Release payment (less any retainage), post to the owner ledger, and close.

grammars.title: Monthly Rent Cycle
grammars.trigger: The monthly rent cycle turns (charges due on the 1st).
grammars.note: The recurring bill-and-receive loop; hands unpaid balances to the collections ladder.

steps.note: Post rent and recurring charges to each tenant ledger.
Send the upcoming-rent reminder to tenants.
Tenant pays rent through the portal.
Apply received payments and reconcile the ledger.
Flag balances still unpaid after the grace period for collections.

grammars.title: Collections Ladder
grammars.trigger: Rent is unpaid past the grace period.
grammars.note: Staged delinquency escalation ending in a pay-or-quit and an eviction decision. Parameterized by late-fee {amount} and statutory {days}.

steps.note: Confirm the balance and apply the late fee of {amount}.
Send a reminder with payment options.
Send a formal past-due notice and offer a payment plan.
Serve the statutory {days}-day pay-or-quit notice.
If still unpaid, decide with the owner whether to file eviction.
Refer to the eviction flow, or record the payment/plan and close.

grammars.title: Lease Violation / Notice to Comply
grammars.trigger: A tenant breaches a non-payment lease term (pet, occupancy, noise, unauthorized alteration).
grammars.note: Cure-or-quit enforcement for curable breaches; escalates to eviction if uncured. Parameterized by {violation} and cure window {days}.

steps.note: Document the {violation} with evidence (photos, reports, inspection).
Confirm it is a genuine lease/rule breach and identify the cure available.
Serve a comply-or-quit notice giving {days} days to correct.
Track whether the tenant cures within the window.
Reinspect to confirm the cure.
Close if cured; escalate to eviction/legal if not.

grammars.title: Eviction (Unlawful Detainer)
grammars.trigger: A tenancy must be terminated through the courts (non-payment or incurable breach).
grammars.note: Court-driven possession recovery, handed to outside counsel and closing into a turn.

steps.note: Confirm owner approval to file and fund legal costs {amount}.
Refer the file to the eviction attorney with ledger and served notices.
Attorney files the unlawful-detainer complaint.
Tenant is served and the court hearing is attended.
Obtain the judgment for possession (and money if sought).
Coordinate the sheriff lockout and secure the unit.
Hand the unit to the make-ready turn flow and pursue any balance.

grammars.title: Lease Renewal
grammars.trigger: A lease is approaching expiration (about 90 days out).
grammars.note: Renewal with owner-approved increase and negotiation; falls through to non-renewal if declined. Day offsets are relative to lease end.

steps.note: The renewal task generates {days} days before the lease ends.
Pull comps and recommend a renewal rent (increase of {amount}).
Owner approves the renewal terms or elects non-renewal.
Send the renewal offer with the new rent and term to the tenant.
Field counteroffers within the owner-approved bounds.
Prepare and e-sign the renewal / amendment.
Update rent, dates, and recurring charges, then close.

grammars.title: Non-Renewal / Notice to Vacate
grammars.trigger: Owner or PM elects not to renew an expiring tenancy.
grammars.note: Compliant wind-down of a tenancy into a scheduled move-out.

steps.note: Owner confirms non-renewal and the reason (sale, owner move-in, turn).
Confirm the required {days}-day notice and no retaliatory or fair-housing issue.
Serve the non-renewal / notice to vacate with the move-out date.
Confirm the tenant's move-out date and schedule the move-out.
Hand to the move-out / turn flow.

grammars.title: Vacancy Marketing
grammars.trigger: A unit is (or soon will be) vacant and rent-ready to market.
grammars.note: Fills a vacancy through listing, showings, and lead handling; loops on weekly price review until leased.

steps.note: Set list rent from comps and confirm {amount} with the owner.
Photograph and write the listing; confirm the unit is rent-ready.
Syndicate the listing to portals and set up self-show / lockbox.
Respond to leads and pre-qualify prospects.
Conduct showings and track traffic and feedback.
Report weekly traffic and recommend a price drop after {days} days without an application.
On interest, hand to the application-screening flow.

grammars.title: Application Screening
grammars.trigger: A prospect submits a rental application.
grammars.note: Fair-housing-safe qualification against written criteria, ending in an approve/decline decision.

steps.note: Collect the completed application and {amount} screening fee from all adults.
Run credit, criminal, eviction, and income/employment checks.
Verify prior-landlord references and income documentation.
Apply the written rental criteria consistently (fair-housing safe).
Notify or obtain owner concurrence where the agreement requires it.
Approve, approve-with-conditions, or issue a written adverse-action decline.
On approval, hand to the lease-execution flow.

grammars.title: Lease Execution
grammars.trigger: An approved applicant is ready to sign a lease.
grammars.note: Turns an approval into a signed, funded lease ready for move-in.

steps.note: Generate the lease with agreed terms, rent, deposit {amount}, and addenda.
Send the lease for e-signature to all leaseholders.
Tenants review and e-sign the lease.
Collect the security deposit and first month's funds (certified).
Countersign on behalf of the owner and distribute copies.
Hand to the move-in flow with the confirmed start date.

grammars.title: Move-In
grammars.trigger: A signed lease has a confirmed start date and cleared funds.
grammars.note: Onboards the tenant into the unit with a documented condition baseline.

steps.note: Confirm the deposit and first rent have cleared before keys release.
Complete a documented move-in condition report with photos.
Tenant reviews and signs the condition report.
Confirm the tenant has transferred utilities into their name.
Release keys/codes and the welcome packet.
Activate the tenant ledger and recurring charges, then close.

grammars.title: Make-Ready Turn
grammars.trigger: A unit is vacated and must be restored to rent-ready.
grammars.note: Scopes and executes the turn between tenancies; hands the finished unit to marketing. Parameterized by {trade} mix and reserve threshold {amount}.

steps.note: Inspect the vacated unit and scope the turn work.
Itemize the make-ready scope (clean, paint, {trade} repairs) and cost {amount}.
Approve any turn costs above the reserve threshold {amount}.
Assign the turn trades and sequence the work.
Complete clean, paint, repairs, and re-key.
Walk the unit to confirm it is rent-ready.
Hand to vacancy-marketing and post turn costs to the owner ledger.

grammars.title: Move-Out Deposit Reconciliation
grammars.trigger: A tenant has vacated and the security deposit must be reconciled.
grammars.note: Statutory deposit disposition, run in parallel with the turn. {days} tokens map to the state's disposition deadline.

steps.note: Compare move-out to move-in condition and document damage beyond normal wear.
Itemize deductions with vendor costs and prorated charges.
Prepare the statutory deposit disposition statement.
Send the disposition and refund the balance (or bill) to the tenant.
If owed beyond the deposit, pursue the balance or send to collections.
Zero and close the tenant ledger.

grammars.title: Routine Inspection
grammars.trigger: A periodic inspection is due (drive-by, mid-lease interior, annual).
grammars.note: Condition inspection with statutory entry notice; feeds work orders and lease-discipline flows. Parameterized by {inspection-type} and notice {days}.

steps.note: Schedule the {inspection-type} inspection and plan tenant notice {days} days ahead.
Serve the statutory entry notice.
Conduct the inspection with photos against a checklist.
Produce the inspection report with findings and ratings.
Spin off work orders for repairs and flag any lease issues.
Send the owner a condition summary.

grammars.title: Insurance Claim
grammars.trigger: Property damage or a liability event may be covered by insurance.
grammars.note: Runs a covered loss from incident through repair and proceeds reconciliation; leans on emergency-response for mitigation.

steps.note: Document the loss (cause, date, photos, injuries).
Notify the owner and file the claim with the carrier.
Dispatch emergency mitigation to prevent further loss.
Meet the adjuster and provide access and documentation.
Obtain repair estimates for the claim.
Manage covered repairs once the claim is approved.
Reconcile claim proceeds, deductible, and repair costs on the owner ledger.

grammars.title: Utility Transfer
grammars.trigger: Utilities must move between tenant, owner, and PM at turnover.
grammars.note: Prevents shutoff during vacancy and confirms tenant transfer at move-in; charges back vacancy utilities to the owner.

steps.note: Identify all utility accounts and the currently responsible party.
Put utilities in the owner/PM name during vacancy to avoid shutoff.
New tenant transfers utilities into their name by move-in.
Confirm the transfer and the final/opening meter reads.
Bill any vacancy utility charges back to the owner ledger and close.

grammars.title: Owner & Property Onboarding
grammars.trigger: A new owner/property is signing on for management.
grammars.note: Brings a new account live: agreement, setup, baseline, and assumption of any existing tenancies.

steps.note: Execute the management agreement and collect owner and property documents.
Gather deed, insurance, keys, warranties, HOA info, and existing leases.
Create the property/owner in the system with reserve {amount} and banking.
Inspect and document the property's baseline condition.
Notify existing tenants, transfer deposits, and assume active leases.
Hand any vacant units to marketing and schedule needed make-ready.
Confirm go-live and send the first owner communication.

grammars.title: Monthly Owner Close
grammars.trigger: The accounting month closes and owners must be paid and reported.
grammars.note: The recurring owner-payout and reporting cycle over the trust ledger; day offsets are day-of-month.

steps.note: Reconcile the trust and operating bank accounts.
Review each owner ledger for correct income and expenses.
Pay outstanding property bills within reserve limits {amount}.
Calculate the owner draw, retaining reserve {amount}.
Send owner payments (ACH) and the management fee.
Generate and publish owner statements with backup.
Field owner questions on the statement.

grammars.title: Owner Offboarding
grammars.trigger: A management agreement is terminated (by owner or PM).
grammars.note: Clean wind-down and handover of an account, closing all ledgers.

steps.note: Log the termination notice and confirm the {days}-day notice period.
Notify tenants of the management change and the new remittance details.
Complete the final owner statement, disburse the balance, and transfer deposits.
Transfer leases, keys, records, and warranties to the owner or new manager.
Deactivate the property and close all ledgers.

catalog.title: Intake & triage a service request
catalog.note: Log the request, gather details and photos, categorize the trade, and route to dispatch or self-help.

catalog.title: After-hours emergency intake & routing
catalog.note: On-call intake and routing of habitability/life-safety calls that arrive outside business hours; the trade emergency leaf it routes to carries the actual emergency response.

catalog.title: Troubleshoot & resolve without dispatch
catalog.note: Guide the tenant through a reset (GFCI, breaker, disposal) or confirm no entry is needed; closes with a single done, no vendor.

catalog.title: Open a general work order
catalog.note: Catch-all dispatch for uncategorized or multi-trade repairs.

catalog.title: Owner approval for over-limit repair
catalog.note: Repairs above the management-agreement limit need the owner's yes before work proceeds.

catalog.title: Clogged or slow drain
catalog.note: Kitchen, bath, or main-line clog cleared.

catalog.title: Running or leaking toilet
catalog.note: Flapper, fill valve, or wax-ring repair.

catalog.title: No hot water
catalog.note: Water-heater pilot, element, or thermostat; escalates to emergency in cold weather.

catalog.title: Dripping faucet or fixture leak
catalog.note: Cartridge, washer, or supply-line repair under a sink or fixture.

catalog.title: Active or burst water leak
catalog.note: Water intrusion in progress; shut off and stop the loss now.

catalog.title: Sewage or main-line backup
catalog.note: Unit uninhabitable until cleared; usually a main-line snake or jet.

catalog.title: Garbage disposal jam or failure
catalog.note: Reset, unjam, or replace the disposal unit.

catalog.title: Water-heater replacement
catalog.note: A larger spend that needs the owner's yes before the install is scheduled.

catalog.title: No cooling / AC out
catalog.note: Loss of cooling in high heat is a habitability emergency.

catalog.title: No heat
catalog.note: Loss of heat in cold is a habitability emergency.

catalog.title: Weak or uneven heating/cooling
catalog.note: System runs but underperforms; airflow, charge, or capacity.

catalog.title: Thermostat malfunction
catalog.note: Dead, miswired, or misconfigured thermostat.

catalog.title: Condensate leak / clogged drain line
catalog.note: Water pooling at the air handler from a clogged condensate line.

catalog.title: Unusual noise or odor
catalog.note: Grinding, squealing, or burning smell from the unit.

catalog.title: Refrigerant leak
catalog.note: Low charge from a leak; find, repair, and recharge.

catalog.title: Outlet or switch not working
catalog.note: Dead receptacle or switch; often a tripped GFCI or a loose connection.

catalog.title: Tripping breaker / partial power loss
catalog.note: Repeated trips or a dead circuit; overload or fault.

catalog.title: Light fixture or ceiling fan issue
catalog.note: Fixture, fan, or ballast repair or replacement.

catalog.title: Smoke/CO detector fault
catalog.note: Chirping, dead, or expired life-safety device; a compliance must-fix.

catalog.title: Full power outage (not utility)
catalog.note: Whole-unit loss of power with the utility confirmed on.

catalog.title: Burning smell or sparking
catalog.note: Hot outlet, smoke, or sparks; fire risk, respond now.

catalog.title: Refrigerator not cooling
catalog.note: Food-loss risk; repair or replace the fridge.

catalog.title: Washer or dryer failure
catalog.note: No-fill, no-drain, no-heat, or no-spin.

catalog.title: Dishwasher failure or leak
catalog.note: No-drain, no-clean, or a leaking dishwasher.

catalog.title: Oven or range not working
catalog.note: No-heat oven or dead burner; a gas smell escalates to emergency.

catalog.title: Built-in microwave failure
catalog.note: Over-range microwave dead or sparking.

catalog.title: Appliance replacement approval
catalog.note: When repair isn't worth it, get the owner's yes to replace.

catalog.title: Door, lock, or rekey
catalog.note: Sticking door, failed lock, or rekey between tenants.

catalog.title: Tenant lockout
catalog.note: Let the tenant back in; often billed back to the tenant at settlement.

catalog.title: Drywall or paint repair
catalog.note: Patch holes, cracks, or a water-stain touch-up.

catalog.title: Window, screen, or blind repair
catalog.note: Broken pane, torn screen, or failed blinds.

catalog.title: Flooring repair
catalog.note: Loose tile, damaged laminate, or torn carpet.

catalog.title: Cabinet, counter, or hardware repair
catalog.note: Loose hinge, broken drawer, or damaged countertop.

catalog.title: Pest or rodent treatment
catalog.note: Reactive treatment for ants, roaches, or rodents.

catalog.title: Roof leak
catalog.note: Active roof leak; tarp and repair before further damage.

catalog.title: Garage door malfunction
catalog.note: Opener, spring, or an off-track door.

catalog.title: Gutter clog or detachment
catalog.note: Overflowing or sagging gutters and downspouts.

catalog.title: Fence or gate repair
catalog.note: Damaged fence section or a failed gate.

catalog.title: Overgrowth or tree work
catalog.note: Reactive trimming, limb removal, or grounds cleanup.

catalog.title: Storm damage insurance claim
catalog.note: Major weather damage filed against the owner's policy.

catalog.title: Roof replacement (capital)
catalog.note: End-of-life roof; competitively bid as a capital project.

catalog.title: Seasonal HVAC tune-up
catalog.note: Spring/fall tune-up to head off summer and winter emergencies.

catalog.title: HVAC filter program
catalog.note: Auto-scheduled filter delivery/swap on a subscription cadence.

catalog.title: Smoke/CO detector test
catalog.note: Annual life-safety test and battery replacement; a compliance obligation.

catalog.title: Gutter cleaning
catalog.note: Clear gutters ahead of the rainy season to prevent water damage.

catalog.title: Recurring landscaping service
catalog.note: Standing lawn/grounds contract billed on a fixed cadence.

catalog.title: Recurring pest control
catalog.note: Standing quarterly pest treatment plan.

catalog.title: Dryer vent cleaning
catalog.note: Annual vent clean to cut fire risk.

catalog.title: Water-heater flush
catalog.note: Annual flush to extend water-heater life.

catalog.title: Set the asking rent for a new vacancy
catalog.note: Run a comparative market analysis and set the list price against active comps and the unit's condition.
catalog.prevalence: every vacancy — the first pricing act on each unit

catalog.title: Reduce the price on a stale listing
catalog.note: Days-on-market drop when inquiries/showings lag the market; the recurring lever during an open vacancy.
catalog.prevalence: ~40-50% of vacancies see at least one reduction

catalog.title: Approve a leasing concession

params.reason: leasing concession (e.g. one month free / waived fee)

catalog.note: A concession spends the owner's money to fill the unit, so it goes up for owner sign-off before it's advertised.
catalog.prevalence: ~15-25% of vacancies in soft markets, near zero in tight ones

catalog.title: Build and syndicate the vacancy listing
catalog.note: Write the copy, set the listing, and syndicate to the ILS/portal network — the spine of marketing a vacancy.
catalog.prevalence: every vacancy — the core marketing word

catalog.title: Order listing photos
catalog.note: Dispatch a paid photographer (occasionally video/matterport) so the listing goes up with real media — a genuine invoiced vendor service.
catalog.prevalence: most vacancies; skipped on quick re-lists that reuse prior photos

catalog.title: Refresh a stale listing
catalog.note: Re-post / bump / rewrite an aging ad to reset its position in the feed and revive impressions.
catalog.prevalence: common on any vacancy open past ~2 weeks

catalog.title: Install the for-rent sign
catalog.note: Place a yard/window sign with a call/text line — still a real lead source for scattered-site SFH. A single done closes it; staff-placed, so no vendor work-order relay.

catalog.title: Take down the listing once leased
catalog.note: Mark the unit rented and pull it from the ILS/portal feeds so leads stop and no one tours an unavailable unit — closes the marketing loop.
catalog.prevalence: every filled vacancy — universal end of the listing lifecycle

catalog.title: Respond to and qualify a prospect inquiry
catalog.note: Intake, pre-qualify (move date, income, pets, occupancy), and route the lead to a showing or off — the lead triage shape.
catalog.prevalence: highest-volume event in the domain — dozens per vacancy

catalog.title: Schedule a showing
catalog.note: Book a tour slot with a qualified prospect (agent-led or self-show window).
catalog.prevalence: a large fraction of qualified inquiries

catalog.title: Issue self-show access
catalog.note: Generate a time-boxed lockbox/smart-lock code after ID verification for unaccompanied self-showings.
catalog.prevalence: dominant showing mode for scattered-site SFH

catalog.title: Follow up after a showing
catalog.note: Post-tour nudge toward an application; capture interest/feedback to inform pricing.
catalog.prevalence: run against most prospects who toured

catalog.title: Intake a rental application
catalog.note: Receive the application and collect the application fee through the portal; open the file for screening.
catalog.prevalence: every applicant — front door to screening

catalog.title: Screen the applicant and render a decision
catalog.note: Run credit/criminal/eviction and income/employment verification against published, fair-housing-compliant criteria; approve, deny, or condition. Income verification and the conditional path are steps of this flow, not separate leaves.
catalog.prevalence: every complete application — the compliance-critical core

catalog.title: Collect a holding deposit
catalog.note: Take the unit off market for an approved applicant against a signed hold agreement; trust-fund handling.
catalog.prevalence: common between approval and lease signing

catalog.title: Issue an adverse action notice
catalog.note: FCRA-compliant denial/adverse-action notice with reasons and the reporting-agency disclosure.
catalog.prevalence: every denial — lower volume, high compliance weight

catalog.title: Generate and e-sign the lease
catalog.note: Populate the lease from the approved terms and route all parties through e-signature — the binding contract act.

catalog.title: Attach required addenda and disclosures
catalog.note: Lead-paint, pet, HOA-rules, mold, bedbug and jurisdiction-specific disclosures bound to the lease before signing.
catalog.prevalence: every lease carries at least the mandated federal/state set

catalog.title: Collect the security deposit and first month
catalog.note: Certified funds for the security deposit and first month cleared before keys — deposit posted to the trust account.
catalog.prevalence: every new tenancy — precondition to move-in

catalog.title: Execute the guarantor agreement
catalog.note: Separate co-signer/guarantor contract when the file was approved with that condition.
catalog.prevalence: tracks conditional approvals — a minority of leases

catalog.title: Coordinate the move-in
catalog.note: Set the move-in date, hand over keys/codes, and complete the welcome — the handoff from vacant to occupied.

catalog.title: Transfer utilities to the new tenant
catalog.note: Confirm the tenant has put utilities in their name (or proof thereof) as of the lease start; close any owner/vacancy account.
catalog.prevalence: every new tenancy where tenant holds utilities

catalog.title: Document the move-in condition
catalog.note: Time-stamped photo/checklist condition report the tenant signs — the baseline that protects the deposit at move-out.

catalog.title: Onboard the tenant to the portal
catalog.note: Create the resident portal login, enroll autopay, and send the welcome packet and how-to-report-maintenance guide.

catalog.title: Run the monthly rent cycle
catalog.note: Generate recurring charges, deliver statements, and receive and post payments for the period. The orchestrating grammar whose steps are the atomic billing rows below.
catalog.prevalence: every active lease, every month — the backbone of the domain

catalog.title: Post a tenant payment
catalog.note: Apply an inbound online/ACH/check payment to the tenant ledger.

catalog.title: Assess a late fee
catalog.note: Apply the lease's late fee once the balance passes the grace date.
catalog.prevalence: ~10-20% of ledgers in a given month

catalog.title: Bill back utilities (RUBS / sub-meter)
catalog.note: Pass owner-paid or common-area utilities to tenants by allocation formula or sub-meter read.
catalog.prevalence: the small-multi subset of leases with utilities in the owner's name

catalog.title: Post a one-time or chargeback charge
catalog.note: Bill the tenant for a lease-permitted cost — key/lockout, tenant-caused repair, or violation fee.
catalog.prevalence: a handful per manager per month

catalog.title: Reverse a returned / NSF payment
catalog.note: Back out a bounced payment, restore the balance, and apply the NSF fee.

catalog.title: Issue a tenant credit or concession
catalog.note: Post an approved credit, fee waiver, or concession to the ledger — touches owner funds, so it is a fiduciary act.
catalog.prevalence: occasional; every one moves owner money

catalog.title: Work a rent delinquency
catalog.note: Escalate an unpaid balance through reminders, phone contact, and statutory pay-or-quit notice.
catalog.prevalence: ~5-8% of leases enter the ladder each month

catalog.title: Handle a partial payment
catalog.note: Decide accept or reject under jurisdiction rules so it doesn't waive a pending notice.

catalog.title: Set up a repayment plan
catalog.note: Negotiate and document a catch-up schedule for a past-due balance.
catalog.prevalence: the share of delinquencies that don't cure in one payment

catalog.title: Pursue a former-tenant balance
catalog.note: Chase a post-move-out balance with demand letters before write-off or agency referral.
catalog.prevalence: on most move-outs that close owing

catalog.title: Refer a balance to collections
catalog.note: Hand an uncollected balance to a third-party agency or credit bureau and write it off the owner's book.
catalog.prevalence: the tail of uncollected former-tenant debt

catalog.title: Lawn / exterior upkeep violation
catalog.note: Notice a tenant to correct overgrown lawn, trash, or exterior neglect — the most common scattered-SFR violation.
catalog.prevalence: the single most frequent SFR lease violation

catalog.title: Unauthorized pet
catalog.note: Address a pet not on the lease — register and fee, or remove.

catalog.title: HOA violation pass-through
catalog.note: Pass an HOA citation to the tenant and track cure before the owner is fined.
catalog.prevalence: on HOA-governed properties — a recurring SFR headache

catalog.title: Unauthorized occupant
catalog.note: Address a long-term guest not named on the lease.

catalog.title: Noise / nuisance complaint
catalog.note: Act on a neighbor or HOA nuisance complaint and notice the tenant to cure.

catalog.title: Housekeeping / property condition
catalog.note: Address an interior condition risking damage or health/safety, often surfaced at inspection.

catalog.title: File a nonpayment eviction
catalog.note: Take an uncured delinquency to unlawful-detainer filing through the owner's counsel.

catalog.title: File a for-cause eviction
catalog.note: Pursue eviction for an uncured or incurable lease violation.

catalog.title: File a holdover eviction
catalog.note: Pursue possession from a tenant who stays past a terminated or expired tenancy — no cause required, distinct from a lease-breach filing.
catalog.prevalence: recurring on month-to-month and post-non-renewal tenancies

catalog.title: Negotiate an eviction stipulation
catalog.note: Document a pay-and-stay or agreed move-out in lieu of judgment.
catalog.prevalence: a meaningful share of filed cases settle here

catalog.title: Coordinate writ of possession / set-out
catalog.note: Schedule the sheriff lockout and set-out after a possession judgment.
catalog.prevalence: the subset of filings that run to judgment

catalog.title: Respond to a tenant inquiry
catalog.note: Answer a non-maintenance question — balance, lease term, policy, portal help, or a tenancy/rent-verification request.
catalog.prevalence: the highest-volume tenant touch in the domain

catalog.title: Resolve a ledger / balance dispute
catalog.note: Research and explain, or correct, a charge the tenant contests.

catalog.title: Update contact or auto-pay details
catalog.note: Change tenant contact information or payment method on file.
catalog.prevalence: routine, self-serve where a portal exists

catalog.title: Verify renters-insurance compliance
catalog.note: Confirm or chase the lease-required renters policy and proof of coverage; escalate to enforcement through the violations system if unmet.

catalog.title: Issue a notice of entry
catalog.note: Serve statutory advance notice before an inspection or vendor visit.
catalog.prevalence: tied to inspection and maintenance volume

catalog.title: Serve a rent-increase notice (month-to-month)
catalog.note: Give statutory notice of a rent change on a periodic tenancy — distinct from a renewal-time increase, which belongs to the leasing/renewal domain.

catalog.title: Complete an estoppel certificate
catalog.note: Certify lease and balance facts for an owner's sale or refinance.

catalog.title: Flag upcoming lease expirations
catalog.note: Standing report surfaces every lease entering its renewal window (typically 90-120 days out) so nothing lapses unhandled.
catalog.prevalence: Runs against every active lease, on schedule

catalog.title: Price the renewing unit and set the increase
catalog.note: Pull comparable rents and unit condition, then fix the renewal rate and the dollar/percent increase — balancing market gain against turnover cost and retention. One pricing motion; feeds the offer.
catalog.prevalence: ~Every renewal gets a pricing look; ~85-90% carry some increase

catalog.title: Get owner direction on renewal terms
catalog.note: Send the owner the recommended rate and the renew / non-renew call for sign-off; it is the owner's asset. Many owners pre-authorize a ceiling and delegate, so this fires only when direction is actually needed (the lease-renewal grammar's owner-sign-off step).

catalog.title: Send a standard renewal offer
catalog.note: The common case: offer a 12-month renewal at a modest market increase.

catalog.title: Offer a flat, no-increase renewal
catalog.note: Hold rent flat to retain a strong-paying tenant or in a soft rental market.

catalog.title: Offer a renewal at market rate
catalog.note: Push a materially below-market rent up toward market on renewal, accepting some turnover risk.

catalog.title: Offer an early renewal
catalog.note: Proactively lock a good tenant well before expiration, often at a favorable rate, to avoid a vacancy.

catalog.title: Chase a non-responding tenant
catalog.note: Automated reminder before the response deadline when a tenant has gone quiet on the offer.

catalog.title: Work a tenant counter or concession request
catalog.note: Tenant counters the offered rent/term, or asks for a repair, upgrade, or rent hold as a condition of renewing; negotiate to terms both sides will sign. This is the lease-renewal grammar's negotiate step, so it carries no completes of its own — it advances the open renewal case rather than opening a new one.
catalog.prevalence: ~25-35% of offers draw a counter or concession ask

catalog.title: Log a tenant's notice to vacate
catalog.note: Tenant declines to renew and gives notice; confirm the vacate date and hand off to the move-out process. No completes here — a tenant's own notice is an intake/log, not the statutory notice the manager serves, and the move-out procedure lives in another domain.
catalog.prevalence: ~A large share of expirations end here

catalog.title: Serve an owner-initiated non-renewal
catalog.note: Owner elects not to renew for sale, family move-in, or major renovation; serve proper notice on the statutory clock (noticeDays set by jurisdiction at binding).

catalog.title: Decline to renew a problem tenancy
catalog.note: Choose not to renew a tenant with chronic late pay or violations where formal eviction is not warranted; document the basis and serve on the statutory clock.

catalog.title: Convert a lapsing lease to month-to-month
catalog.note: Roll an unsigned or short-horizon tenancy to month-to-month, usually at a premium, keeping the option to end on short notice. The premium is pushed to the ledger by the standard renewal rent update.

catalog.title: Resolve a holdover tenant
catalog.note: Tenant remains past lease end with no signed renewal; force a resolution — sign, convert to MTM, or serve notice down the statutory path.

catalog.title: Execute the renewal addendum
catalog.note: Prepare and e-sign the addendum extending the existing lease at the agreed terms — the default paper for an accepted renewal.

catalog.title: Push the renewed rent into the ledger
catalog.note: Update the scheduled rent and lease dates so monthly billing picks up the new terms automatically — also applies the month-to-month premium on MTM conversions.

catalog.title: Execute a full renewal lease
catalog.note: Some owners or jurisdictions require a fresh lease at renewal rather than an addendum; paper the whole document anew.

catalog.title: Process approved tenant into the unit
catalog.note: The full move-in run: clear funds, inspect condition, transfer utilities, hand over keys, orient the tenant.

catalog.title: Confirm and schedule the move-in date
catalog.note: Possession date set in writing, aligned to lease start and make-ready completion.

catalog.title: Confirm the unit is make-ready before possession
catalog.note: Final walk that the turn is finished and the unit is clean, safe, and habitable before keys release.
catalog.prevalence: ~70% — units coming off a turn rather than new/owner-ready

catalog.title: Deliver welcome packet and tenant orientation
catalog.note: How to pay rent, submit maintenance, reach the PM, plus house rules and emergency contacts.

catalog.title: Set up tenant portal and payment account
catalog.note: Portal invite sent; autopay enrollment and contact info captured.

catalog.title: Capture tenant contact, vehicle, and emergency information
catalog.note: Phone, email, occupants, vehicles, and emergency contact recorded to the tenant record at onboarding.

catalog.title: Notify owner the unit is occupied
catalog.note: Owner told move-in is complete; property status flips vacant to occupied.

catalog.title: Verify move-in funds cleared
catalog.note: First month, deposit, and fees must clear as certified funds before keys release — no personal check on the way in.

catalog.title: Post security deposit to the trust ledger
catalog.note: Deposit booked to the trust/escrow ledger, never owner operating cash.

catalog.title: Start the rent ledger and recurring charges
catalog.note: Recurring rent, pet rent, and any billed-back utilities initialized from the lease start date; the monthly rent cycle takes over in steady state.

catalog.title: Calculate prorated first-month rent
catalog.note: Prorate by move-in day and net against monies already collected at signing.

catalog.title: Collect pet deposit / pet fee
catalog.note: Per the pet addendum; refundable deposit and non-refundable fee posted to the correct ledgers.

catalog.title: Complete the move-in condition inspection report
catalog.note: Room-by-room, photographed condition report — the baseline the move-out deposit reconciliation is measured against.

catalog.title: Obtain tenant sign-off on the condition report
catalog.note: Tenant reviews, adds exceptions, and signs within the state's disclosure window.

catalog.title: Test smoke/CO detectors and safety devices
catalog.note: Detectors, GFCIs, and door locks verified operational and dated at possession.

catalog.title: Open punch-list items found at move-in
catalog.note: Minor defects the tenant flags at move-in dispatched as routine work orders.

catalog.title: Transfer utilities into the tenant's name
catalog.note: Tenant-responsible utilities moved into their name as of the lease start date.

catalog.title: Confirm proof of utility activation
catalog.note: Tenant provides account numbers or confirmation before keys, so no gap in service.

catalog.title: Close owner/PM placeholder utility accounts
catalog.note: Stop the vacancy-period owner/PM accounts as of the move-in date.

catalog.title: Hand over keys and access devices
catalog.note: Door keys, mailbox key, garage remotes, and fobs issued and logged at possession.

catalog.title: Rekey locks before possession
catalog.note: Locks rekeyed between tenancies per company policy and, in many states, statute.

catalog.title: Program smart-lock and gate codes
catalog.note: Unique tenant entry codes generated and issued; prior vacancy/showing codes revoked.
catalog.prevalence: ~35% — units with smart locks or gated communities

catalog.title: Deliver required move-in disclosures
catalog.note: Lead-paint, mold, bedbug, and state/local move-in disclosures delivered and acknowledged.

catalog.title: Collect proof of renters insurance
catalog.note: Policy meeting the required liability limit, with the PM/owner listed as an interested party.

catalog.title: Execute pet addendum and register the pet
catalog.note: Pet screening, signed addendum, and any ESA/service-animal documentation recorded.

catalog.title: Register tenant with HOA, parking, and gate
catalog.note: HOA tenant registration, parking permits, and amenity/gate access filed.

catalog.title: Process notice to vacate
catalog.note: Log the tenant's written notice, confirm required days per lease/state, and set the move-out date.

catalog.title: Send move-out instructions packet
catalog.note: Auto-send the move-out checklist, cleaning expectations, key-return process and forwarding-address request.

catalog.title: Confirm possession / key return
catalog.note: Collect keys, remotes and access devices; confirm the unit is surrendered and vacant.

catalog.title: Place utilities on owner/vacancy hold
catalog.note: Roll power/water/gas into the owner's or PM's name so service stays live through the turn. (Param tokens inferred; reconcile at the gate.)

catalog.title: Handle early termination / lease break
catalog.note: Apply buyout/re-let terms, quantify the fee, and get owner sign-off on releasing the tenant early. No lease-break/owner-release grammar exists in the library yet, so this runs as a firm human task (do NOT mis-bind to owner-approval-for-spend — a tenant buyout is the opposite money direction from a PM spend approval).

catalog.title: Move-out inspection
catalog.note: Photo-document unit condition at surrender against the move-in report — the basis for separating ordinary wear from chargeable damage and for scoping the turn.

catalog.title: Pre-move-out (initial) inspection
catalog.note: Statutory walk-through offered before departure (e.g. CA) so the tenant can cure before deductions.
catalog.prevalence: ~15-25% (where the tenant requests or statute requires)

catalog.title: Reconcile & disburse security deposit
catalog.note: Make the wear-vs-damage determination against the move-in baseline, itemize deductions, produce the disposition statement, and refund the balance from the deposit trust account within the statutory window. The refund IS the terminal step of this grammar — not a separate task. (deadlineDays token inferred.)

catalog.title: Handle deposit deduction dispute
catalog.note: Respond to a tenant contesting the itemized statement; support the charges with documentation or adjust before escalation.

catalog.title: Run the make-ready turn
catalog.note: The umbrella: coordinate the full punch list from vacant to rent-ready against a target turn time, spawning the trade work orders below. (Param tokens inferred.)

catalog.title: Rekey / change locks
catalog.note: Rekey all entry locks between tenancies — a standing liability and habitability requirement, held firm on liability grounds.

catalog.title: Turn cleaning
catalog.note: Deep clean the vacant unit including appliances, baths and fixtures.

catalog.title: Punch-list repairs
catalog.note: Knock out drywall, fixtures, hardware and miscellaneous fixes flagged at inspection.

catalog.title: Interior paint
catalog.note: Touch-up or full repaint to freshen walls between tenancies.

catalog.title: Owner approval for turn scope
catalog.note: Route turn bids over the management-agreement limit to the owner for approval before work starts. (Param tokens inferred.)

catalog.title: Grounds / exterior make-ready
catalog.note: Yard cleanup, mow/edge, debris haul and exterior tidy before re-listing — a real recurring line item on scattered-site single-family turns.

catalog.title: Carpet / flooring service
catalog.note: Professional carpet clean, or replace flooring worn beyond ordinary use.

catalog.title: Rent-ready sign-off inspection
catalog.note: Final walk confirming the unit meets rent-ready standard (including detectors/safety items) before it goes back to market — the terminal gate of the turn.

catalog.title: Final account statement
catalog.note: Close the tenant ledger: prorated rent, utility charge-backs, unpaid balances and net deposit result.

catalog.title: Bill damage beyond deposit
catalog.note: Post chargeable damage exceeding the deposit to the tenant ledger with supporting documentation.

catalog.title: Send move-out balance to collections
catalog.note: Escalate an unrecovered final balance through demand and third-party collections/reporting. (balanceType token inferred.)

catalog.title: Release rent-ready unit to leasing
catalog.note: Hand the rent-ready unit to leasing to price and list, closing the turn into a new vacancy cycle. (Param tokens inferred.)

catalog.title: Report turn cost & disposition to owner
catalog.note: Summarize turn spend, deposit outcome and rent-ready date for the owner; feeds the monthly owner statement.

catalog.title: Owner election: re-rent vs. sell/hold
catalog.note: Capture the owner's decision to re-lease, sell, or hold the unit vacant after the turn; a sell election forks out to owner-offboarding.

catalog.title: Monthly three-way trust reconciliation
catalog.note: Bank balance tied out to the book balance and the sum of owner ledgers; the opening pass that triggers the month-end owner close cascade.
catalog.prevalence: monthly, every trust account — the signature fiduciary task

catalog.title: Returned / NSF payment reversal
catalog.note: A bounced tenant or owner payment reversed and the affected ledgers re-struck so trust never reflects money it never held.
catalog.prevalence: ~30-40% of trust exceptions; the most common

catalog.title: Negative owner balance correction
catalog.note: An owner ledger driven negative is caught and cured before any disbursement leaves the trust account.

catalog.title: Misapplied receipt correction
catalog.note: A payment posted to the wrong property or owner is moved to the correct ledger and both sides re-struck.

catalog.title: Stale outstanding item clearance
catalog.note: Uncleared checks and aged deposits surfaced at reconciliation are chased down, then voided or re-issued.

catalog.title: Pay a vendor invoice
catalog.note: A maintenance or service invoice within owner-authorized limits, matched to its work order, paid on the next disbursement run.

catalog.title: Pay a recurring property bill
catalog.note: Mortgage, HOA dues, utilities, and other scheduled obligations paid from owner funds each cycle.
catalog.prevalence: monthly, every property with bills on file

catalog.title: Pay property tax or insurance premium
catalog.note: Property-tax installments and insurance premiums paid on their due dates, with owner funding confirmed first.
catalog.prevalence: semi-annual / annual; timing-critical, penalty on a miss

catalog.title: Hold a bill for insufficient owner funds
catalog.note: The exception decision: a bill that would overdraw the owner is held, and the owner is asked to fund it or the reserve draw is set in motion (executed in reserves.draw-for-bill).

catalog.title: Pay a one-off owner-directed bill
catalog.note: A one-time disbursement the owner specifically directs on their behalf — special assessment, contribution, or the like — set up and released.

catalog.title: Release the monthly owner draw
catalog.note: Net proceeds swept to the owner by ACH once the reserve floor is satisfied.
catalog.prevalence: monthly, every owner in good standing

catalog.title: Deliver the owner statement
catalog.note: The month's income-and-expense owner statement rendered and posted to the owner portal.

catalog.title: Post the management fee
catalog.note: The management fee computed on collected rent and posted against the owner ledger each cycle.

catalog.title: Resolve an owner statement inquiry
catalog.note: An owner questions a charge, fee, or draw on their statement; the ledger is researched, explained, and corrected if warranted.
catalog.prevalence: monthly, a steady share of owners — a core owner-relations touch

catalog.title: Process an off-cycle owner draw
catalog.note: An early or extra disbursement the owner requests outside the normal cycle, checked against reserves first.

catalog.title: Issue year-end 1099 and owner tax packet
catalog.note: Owner 1099-MISC and the annual income/expense summary generated and issued at year-end.

catalog.title: Owner approval for a repair over the limit
catalog.note: A repair above the management-agreement limit sent to the owner for sign-off before the vendor is dispatched.
catalog.prevalence: any work order over the owner's limit — the most common approval

catalog.title: Ratify emergency spend after the fact
catalog.note: Emergency work already done to protect the property, presented to the owner after the fact for ratification (no pre-approval gate applies).

catalog.title: Authorize a recurring service contract
catalog.note: Ongoing service — landscaping, pool, pest — authorized by the owner before the first invoice.

catalog.title: Owner sign-off on a capital project
catalog.note: Roof, HVAC replacement, or full repaint: multiple bids gathered and presented for owner selection and sign-off.

catalog.title: Request owner funding for a reserve shortfall
catalog.note: When proceeds can't restore the reserve floor, the owner is asked to contribute to bring it back up.

catalog.title: Replenish the reserve from proceeds
catalog.note: The reserve topped back to its floor out of the next cycle's proceeds after a draw-down.

catalog.title: Draw the reserve to cover a bill
catalog.note: The funding action: the reserve is tapped to cover an approved bill the operating balance can't (often following a bill-pay hold), then flagged for replenishment.
catalog.prevalence: ~whenever a bill exceeds available operating funds

catalog.title: Adjust the reserve target
catalog.note: The reserve floor raised or lowered by owner agreement as the portfolio, season, or risk changes.

catalog.title: Stand up a new owner's accounting

params.scope: full — trust sub-ledger, opening reserve, ACH banking, fee schedule

catalog.note: A new owner's accounting stood up: trust sub-ledger, opening reserve, ACH banking, and fee terms recorded.

catalog.title: Close out a departing owner
catalog.note: A departing owner's final accounting: last statement, final draw, reserve return, and ledger close-out.

catalog.title: Add a property to an existing owner

params.scope: add-property — new sub-ledger and reserve, existing banking

catalog.note: An additional door brought under an existing owner: new sub-ledger and reserve on the banking already on file.

catalog.title: Update owner payout banking
catalog.note: An owner's ACH/draw banking changed and verified out-of-band before any funds route to it — the primary defense against payout fraud.

catalog.title: Apply a management fee change
catalog.note: A change to the fee schedule or terms mid-relationship applied to the owner's ledger going forward.

catalog.title: Serve notice of entry
catalog.note: Statutory advance notice (typically 24-48h) before entering an occupied unit for repairs, inspections, or showings.

catalog.title: Serve notice to pay rent or quit
catalog.note: First formal statutory step toward eviction once a tenant is delinquent past the grace period.

catalog.title: Serve notice to comply (lease violation)
catalog.note: Unauthorized occupant or pet, nuisance, or other curable covenant breach; demands cure or vacatur.

catalog.title: Serve notice of rent increase
catalog.note: Statutory advance notice of a rent change, timed to the jurisdiction's required lead days.

catalog.title: Serve for-cause lease termination notice
catalog.note: Termination for a serious or incurable breach where no cure is offered before filing.

catalog.title: Process belief-of-abandonment notice
catalog.note: Statutory notice of belief of abandonment before reclaiming a unit and disposing of left property.

catalog.title: File eviction for non-payment
catalog.note: Unlawful detainer after the pay-or-quit period lapses; the dominant eviction ground.

catalog.title: File eviction for holdover
catalog.note: Tenant remains past a valid termination or non-renewal notice.

catalog.title: File eviction for material lease violation
catalog.note: Unlawful detainer following an uncured comply-or-quit notice.

catalog.title: Negotiate payment / move-out stipulation
catalog.note: Court-adjacent settlement staying the eviction on a payment plan or an agreed vacate date.

catalog.title: Coordinate writ of possession & set-out
catalog.note: Schedule the sheriff lockout and take possession after judgment for the landlord.

catalog.title: Process assistance / service animal request
catalog.note: Verify a disability-related need and grant a reasonable exception to pet policy and fees.

catalog.title: Review reasonable accommodation request
catalog.note: Run and document the interactive process for a policy/practice accommodation.

catalog.title: Approve & coordinate reasonable modification
catalog.note: Approve a physical unit modification (grab bars, ramp) and, where landlord-coordinated, dispatch the work at the appropriate party's cost.

catalog.title: Review listing copy for fair-housing compliance
catalog.note: Screen marketing language for protected-class, steering, or occupancy-limit issues before publish.

catalog.title: Respond to fair-housing complaint or agency inquiry
catalog.note: Preserve records and respond to a HUD / state civil-rights agency complaint; loop in counsel.

catalog.title: Respond to warranty-of-habitability repair demand
catalog.note: Statutory repair demand carrying repair-and-deduct or rent-withhold risk; dispatched under the clock.

catalog.title: Cure municipal code-enforcement violation
catalog.note: Abate a cited housing/health-code violation before the enforcement deadline to avoid fines.

catalog.title: Restore essential service (heat/water/electric)
catalog.note: Statutory habitability emergency: an essential service is out and must be restored immediately.

catalog.title: Address mold / moisture habitability complaint
catalog.note: Investigate the moisture source and remediate; documentation matters for liability.

catalog.title: Address infestation habitability complaint
catalog.note: Bed-bug, roach, or rodent statutory abatement; treatment and follow-up.

catalog.title: Handle lead-based paint disclosure / hazard
catalog.note: Deliver the federal disclosure and EPA pamphlet at lease-up and respond to any lead hazard in pre-1978 housing.

catalog.title: File / renew municipal rental registration
catalog.note: Register the unit with the city/county rental program; annual or biennial where required.

catalog.title: Schedule & pass municipal rental inspection
catalog.note: Proactive inspection required to obtain or keep the rental license; correct and re-inspect on fail.

catalog.title: File smoke / CO detector certification
catalog.note: Certify working smoke and carbon-monoxide detectors at lease-up or point of sale where required.

catalog.title: Schedule & pass housing-voucher (HQS/NSPIRE) inspection
catalog.note: Recurring housing-authority inspection required to keep the HAP contract on a voucher-holding tenancy; correct and re-inspect on fail.

catalog.title: Renew local rental business / occupancy license
catalog.note: Keep the per-property business or certificate-of-occupancy license current.

catalog.title: File rent-control / stabilization registration
catalog.note: Register the unit and its current legal rent in a rent-regulated jurisdiction.

catalog.title: Reconcile trust / escrow account (three-way)
catalog.note: Monthly three-way reconciliation of the trust bank balance, book balance, and owner/tenant liabilities.

catalog.title: Return / dispose security deposit within statute
catalog.note: Itemize deductions and refund or withhold within the statutory deadline to avoid penalty exposure.

catalog.title: Verify deposit holding & interest compliance
catalog.note: Confirm deposits sit in the correct account type with any required interest accrual and disclosure.

catalog.title: Review owner-fund segregation / anti-commingling
catalog.note: Confirm broker and owner funds stay segregated per license law; no commingling.

catalog.title: Process unclaimed funds / escheatment
catalog.note: Report and remit stale uncashed owner or tenant funds to the state per dormancy rules.

catalog.title: Respond to state trust-account audit / exam
catalog.note: Produce records and respond to a real-estate commission trust-account examination.

catalog.title: Renew broker / firm license
catalog.note: Renew the designated broker and property-management company license before expiration.

catalog.title: Track continuing-education compliance
catalog.note: Monitor each licensee's CE hours against the hours required for their next renewal.

catalog.title: Renew salesperson / leasing agent licenses
catalog.note: Keep each leasing agent's real-estate license active and affiliated with the brokerage.

catalog.title: Renew E&O / general liability coverage
catalog.note: Maintain the errors-and-omissions and liability insurance the license and owners require.

catalog.title: File entity annual report / registered agent
catalog.note: Keep the LLC or corporation in good standing with the Secretary of State.

catalog.title: Semi-annual interior condition inspection
catalog.note: Scheduled mid-lease walk of the unit interior for condition, wear, and lease compliance.
catalog.prevalence: ~40% of interior inspections; the default periodic check

catalog.title: New-tenant interior check (60-90 day)
catalog.note: Early first-year walk to confirm a new tenant is caring for the property.

catalog.title: For-cause / complaint-driven interior inspection
catalog.note: Entry walk triggered by a neighbor complaint or a suspected violation (unauthorized occupant/pet, sublet, condition concern), before it is documented.

catalog.title: Document lease violation found on interior inspection
catalog.note: Unauthorized pet or occupant, smoking, or housekeeping/health-safety concern documented and noticed.

catalog.title: Interior inspection refused or no-access
catalog.note: Tenant denied entry or was a no-show; re-notice and reschedule.

catalog.title: Periodic exterior drive-by inspection
catalog.note: Curbside pass to check exterior condition, occupancy signs, and upkeep without entering.

catalog.title: Document exterior/curb violation
catalog.note: Overgrown lawn, trash, or unauthorized vehicle noticed to the tenant to cure.

catalog.title: Process HOA / municipal violation notice
catalog.note: HOA or city violation letter received; pass the cure obligation to tenant or owner.

catalog.title: Drive-by check of vacant / owner-held property
catalog.note: Security and condition pass on an unoccupied property between tenancies.

catalog.title: Post-storm exterior damage sweep
catalog.note: Rapid exterior look after severe weather to catch roof, tree, or fence damage.

catalog.title: Annual comprehensive property inspection
catalog.note: Full interior-and-exterior condition walk with photos, the anchor once-a-year inspection. The owner report is the grammar's closing step, not a separate task.

catalog.title: Smoke/CO detector & life-safety check
catalog.note: Verify and document detectors, GFCIs, and egress for habitability compliance.

catalog.title: Flag capital improvement need for owner approval
catalog.note: Roof, HVAC replacement, or similar big-ticket item surfaced from findings for owner sign-off.

catalog.title: Recommend preventive service from findings
catalog.note: Gutter cleaning, HVAC tune-up, or caulking recommended off the annual walk — the recommendation handoff, not the service execution.

catalog.title: Coordinate insurance carrier inspection
catalog.note: Schedule access and meet the carrier's underwriting/loss-control inspector.

catalog.title: Cure insurance inspection deficiency
catalog.note: Fix carrier-flagged items (loose handrail, roof, overhanging tree) before the policy binds or renews.

catalog.title: Coordinate 4-point / wind-mitigation inspection
catalog.note: Order and host the licensed inspector for the carrier's 4-point or wind-mit form (regional — coastal/older-stock markets).

catalog.title: Coordinate lender / REO inspection
catalog.note: Occupancy and condition verification requested by a lender or REO servicer.

catalog.title: Coordinate Section 8 HQS / NSPIRE inspection
catalog.note: Schedule access and meet the housing authority inspector for a voucher unit.

catalog.title: Cure HQS / NSPIRE fail items
catalog.note: Repair fail items and pass re-inspection to keep the housing-assistance payment flowing.

catalog.title: Coordinate municipal rental license inspection
catalog.note: City/county rental registration or licensing inspection to keep the unit legally rentable.

catalog.title: Respond to code-enforcement citation
catalog.note: Abate a municipal code violation within the compliance deadline to avoid fines.

catalog.title: Coordinate lead-based paint / EPA inspection
catalog.note: Lead risk assessment or clearance on a pre-1978 unit, often tied to turnover or a child in residence.

catalog.title: Seasonal winterization / freeze-prep inspection
catalog.note: Pre-winter readiness walk of heat, pipe insulation, and exterior faucets to catch freeze exposure; the actual winterization service is dispatched as maintenance.

catalog.title: Pre-storm / hurricane readiness inspection
catalog.note: Pre-season readiness pass for shutters, drainage, and loose exterior items.

catalog.title: Re-inspect to verify a prior finding cured
catalog.note: Return visit confirming a documented violation or condition was corrected.

catalog.title: Convert inspection findings into work orders
catalog.note: Turn the punch list from any inspection into triaged, dispatchable repairs — the single findings-to-repairs handoff for the whole domain.

catalog.title: Verify vendor completed inspection-flagged repair
catalog.note: Quality check that the dispatched fix actually resolved the flagged condition.

catalog.title: New Owner & Property Onboarding
catalog.note: Execute the management agreement for a brand-new owner and stand up their first property end-to-end.
catalog.prevalence: ~45% of onboarding starts (each new owner relationship)

catalog.title: Add Property for Existing Owner
catalog.note: Bring an additional door under an existing owner's agreement — same intake, owner record already in place.
catalog.prevalence: ~30% of onboarding starts (existing owners adding doors)

catalog.title: Management Agreement Renewal
catalog.note: Annual PMA term rolls or auto-renews; flag any that require a signed re-up.

catalog.title: Agreement Amendment / Fee Change
catalog.note: Amend fee schedule, managed-property list, or terms mid-term with a signed addendum.

catalog.title: Owner Record & Tax Setup
catalog.note: Create the owner entity, contacts, ownership split, and collect a W-9 for 1099 reporting.

catalog.title: Owner Disbursement (ACH) Setup
catalog.note: Capture and verify owner banking so monthly draws pay out of the trust account by ACH.

catalog.title: Initial Operating Reserve Funding
catalog.note: Collect the agreement's minimum reserve into trust so early repairs and bills can clear.

catalog.title: Owner Insurance Verification
catalog.note: Collect the landlord/dwelling policy and confirm the PM is named additional insured.

catalog.title: Owner Portal Invite & Statement Delivery
catalog.note: Send the owner-portal invite and set electronic statement/1099 delivery preferences.

catalog.title: Property & Unit Record Setup
catalog.note: Build the property/unit record — address, beds/baths, systems, appliances, GL coding.

catalog.title: Onboarding Condition Inspection
catalog.note: Full interior/exterior condition inspection with photos to baseline the property.

catalog.title: Key & Access Collection
catalog.note: Collect keys, remotes, garage/gate codes, and install a lockbox for vacant units.

catalog.title: Compliance & Registration Setup
catalog.note: Pre-1978 lead disclosure, smoke/CO check, and any local rental registration or business license.

catalog.title: Utility Setup / Transfer
catalog.note: Put utilities in owner/PM name while vacant, or verify tenant accounts if occupied.

catalog.title: HOA & Warranty Setup
catalog.note: Record HOA contacts/rules/dues and any appliance or home-warranty coverage.

catalog.title: Initial Make-Ready
catalog.note: Bring a vacant newly-managed unit to rent-ready before marketing.

catalog.title: Tenant Transfer Notice
catalog.note: Notify in-place tenants of the new manager and where/how to pay rent going forward.

catalog.title: Lease & Estoppel Collection
catalog.note: Collect in-place leases and confirm terms, rent, and dates via a signed tenant estoppel.

catalog.title: Security Deposit Transfer
catalog.note: Receive held tenant deposits from the prior owner/manager into the trust account.

catalog.title: Rent Roll Reconciliation
catalog.note: Reconcile assumed rent roll — balances, prepaid rent, concessions, and delinquencies.

catalog.title: Tenant Ledger & Recurring Charge Setup
catalog.note: Stand up recurring rent charges and opening ledger balances for each assumed tenant.

catalog.title: Owner Termination
catalog.note: Owner ends the agreement (or PM terminates) — run the wind-down and final handoff.

catalog.title: Property Sale Offboarding
catalog.note: Owner sells the property — coordinate with buyer/escrow, prorations, and tenant handoff.

catalog.title: Final Owner Accounting
catalog.note: Final trust reconciliation, reserve return, closing statement, and year-end 1099.

catalog.title: Deposit & Records Handoff
catalog.note: Transfer held tenant deposits, leases, keys, and records to the owner or new manager.

catalog.title: Tenant Offboarding Notice
catalog.note: Notify tenants of the management change and new payment/contact instructions.
